content.text: All preferred elements appear satisfied. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: Section 13 meets the preferred position in full. The subscription grant in 13.1 runs to Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf (no written-notice condition needed), and 13.2 gives Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence for paid-up software, Vendor Technology and embedded Deliverable material (confirmed by 14.3). Section 13.3 bars Vendor revocation or suspension except for a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a cure opportunity, and no other suspension or Vendor convenience-termination right exists (Section 9 limits Vendor to material breach and insolvency). Licence rights are transferable to an Affiliate or successor via Section 24, and Section 24.1 expressly permits Customer assignment without Vendor consent to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets. "Customer" is the named entity and "Affiliate" is defined broadly on a control test, so affiliate coverage is real rather than nominal. No redline is warranted.
